subject: Business Models
title: Kozmo.com: Free Delivery Illusion
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Kozmo.com: Free Delivery Illusion.

hook.text: Kozmo.com delivered anything—DVDs, snacks, Starbucks—in under an hour for free. No delivery fee. No minimum order.

buildup.text: Customers could order a single candy bar and get free delivery. The service was wildly popular in New York.

discovery.text: Each delivery cost Kozmo $10-15. Average order value was $12. The math was catastrophically negative.

twist.text: Kozmo tried to add a minimum order and delivery fee. Users, trained to expect free delivery, abandoned the service.

climax.text: Training customers on an unsustainable price is a one-way trip. You can't easily add costs users never expected.

punchline.text: One candy bar, free delivery. You can't charge for what you gave away.

quiz.question: Why couldn't Kozmo.com fix its model by adding delivery fees?
options: Customers trained on free delivery left when fees were added

details.summary: Kozmo.com promised free one-hour delivery of small items like DVDs, snacks, and magazines in the early 2000s. Without delivery fees or minimum order values, every delivery lost money. The company burned through 280 million dollars before shutting down in 2001.
details.whyItMatters: Kozmo.com demonstrated that free delivery of low-value items is economically impossible. Its failure previewed the delivery economics challenges that still plague modern instant delivery startups like Gopuff and Gorillas twenty years later.
takeaways: Free one-hour delivery of small items lost money on virtually every order
No minimum order value meant many deliveries cost more than the order total
280 million dollars burned before shutting down without finding sustainable economics

faq.question: Why doesn't free delivery work for small everyday items?
faq.answer: Last-mile delivery costs 5 to 15 dollars per trip regardless of order size. When a customer orders a 3-dollar snack with free delivery, the company loses money on every transaction. Without minimum order values or delivery fees, higher volume only means faster cash burn.

faq.question: How do modern delivery services try to avoid Kozmo's mistakes?
faq.answer: They charge delivery fees, set minimum order amounts, charge subscriptions for free delivery, increase basket sizes through product recommendations, use dark stores for faster picking, and rely on gig workers instead of employed drivers to variabilize delivery costs.
